## Summary

The gated attention block serves the Flash-Next / QSA **decode step over a paged KV cache**: a dense `[B, S_q]` declaration on a
`QsaSpec` geometry (`causal_bottom_right=True`) with `kv_source="paged"`, `paged_kv_page_size=P` and the pools' and block table's
samples.  The step's tokens are written through into the pools (and the raw indexer key into `index_k_raw` when the band is declared),
then stage (4) is the Rubin index-list sparse core **reading the pools** (`sdpa/fwd/sparse_gqa_sm107`'s paged read on the
bottom-right diagonal): per sequence the listed 4-token blocks plus the open tail over the first `kv_lens[b]` tokens of
`block_table[b]`, row `j` at position `kv_lens[b] - S_q + j`.

* **The list form is a declaration fact derived from `S_q`.**  At `S_q <= 4` ONE list per sequence -- `execute(block_ids=)`
  `[B, top_k]` int32 (+ `block_lens [B]`), selected at the step-0 position `kv_lens[b] - S_q` and shared by the step's rows: a
  speculative (MTP) row sees the listed blocks plus every token from the step-0 tail start to its own position (the contract page's
  definition; the adapter's `list_per_sequence` arm).  Past four rows one list per row (`[B, S_q, top_k]` / `[B x S_q, top_k]`) at
  bottom-right positions: a chunked prefill / prefix-cache hit over the pools, at any `S_q` (the sparse core runs one work item per
  query row: no 32-row cap, no decode-tile route).
* **`decode_split_kv`** is the one performance knob: `None` = the fill rule `ceil(SMs / (B x H_kv x S_q))` capped at the item's
  tile count `ceil((top_k + 1) / 32)`, or a pinned int in that range; fp32 partials inside `get_workspace_size()`, the split combine
  as a second launch; the same function under every value.  `fuse_gate` is served at every split (the core's epilogue unsplit, the
  combine otherwise); `return_lse` is served (`[B, H_q, S_q]` fp32).
* **Typed declines** (each naming its feature, every one pinned): the packed (`thd=True`) form over the pools -- the serving table's
  `sparse` row now reads "the sparse core serves packed sequences and paged pools one at a time"; a block-table sample that is not
  contiguous (the core binds the whole `[B, max_pages]` table; `execute(block_table=)` is exactly that table); a split past the
  item's tile count; `fuse_prepare`; the in-block indexer over the pools; `causal_bottom_right` on the block's own K / V now names
  this mode.  `_EXTEND_DECLINES`' `decode_rows` and `return_lse` rows exempt `QsaSpec` geometries; `serving_envelope(...).decode`
  gains `sparse_core` (appended) and spells both list forms in `requires`; `routes` is empty for a sparse geometry (the dense tile's
  facts do not apply).
* **Two execute-path details the cells caught**: at `S_q = 1` torch's `.view` gives the unit seq dim a stride that differs from the
  declared one and the adapter's exact `_bind` refused it -- the sparse stage now re-strides UNIT dims of its bound views to the
  declaration (an exact view; a non-unit mismatch stays the typed refusal); the serving declaration's capture-safe projections exist
  only for an `N` that 256 divides, so the indexer band (+640 columns) keeps the driver's route (eager steps; a capture is the
  driver's typed refusal at the first captured execute) instead of declining the whole block at compile.
* **The MTP matrix of the standalone sparse decode form** (the kernel-side cells cut out of the sparse-core PR as planned): every
  residue of the step-0 position at `S_q` 1..4, the shared list bitwise the replicated per-token list plus the completed block
  appended explicitly, the `S_q = 5` boundary decline, and the tracker's MTP wording with the bytes per step.

No kernel, barrier, ring or SMEM change: the mode binds the sparse core's served arms (`bottom_right` / `list_per_sequence` /
`split_kv` / `paged_kv`).  The `SparseCapabilities` record's fields do not move (its `decode` comment names the block); the
tracker's serving-forms section, index-list section, feature row and gaps rows and the doc page's contract table, decode-mode
paragraph, decode-form section and limits bullets flip in the same commit.

## Tests

`test/python/gated_attention_block/cutedsl/test_block_qsa_decode.py` (new, L0).  Host cells (any device): the declaration facts
(the list form per `S_q`, no dense route, where the gate runs, the split rule, the capture-safe projections per geometry), the typed
declines, the static envelope, the execute-time form checks on an uncompiled block under `set_sync_debug_mode("error")` (the 16-byte
base-alignment refusal of `block_ids` before any stage on both list forms, with an aligned storage-offset control -- a review item), the split
rule.  Rubin cells (cc 10.7, a development node, 204 SMs; functional, no perf claim): the decode ladder -- 9 cells, `S_q` 1..4 shared
and 8 / 64 per row, `B` 1 / 2 / 4, `kv_lens` 2 .. 20000 with a dead entry and a sequence shorter than the step, pages 16 / 32 / 64
on HND / NHD / unified pools, bf16 / f16, splits 1 / 2 / 4 / 17 and the rule, the gate fused and separate, the LSE, the indexer
band's raw-key write-through, the 24 / 2 geometry at `d_model` 2560 -- against the fp32 oracle of the WHOLE sequence (the dense block
reference's post-norm / post-RoPE Q, K, V and gate; the prefix rows fill NaN pools, the step rows are the block's own write-through;
the step rows' attention over `qsa_visible_mask(..., pos0=)`): `cos(out) >= 0.99998`, the gated O within 3.9e-3 bf16 / 3.1e-5 f16
(the suite's `atol 2e-2`, never widened), the LSE within 7.3e-5, dead rows exactly `0` / `-inf`, the pools' step rows BITWISE the
slab's K / V bands, the prefix rows and the NULL block untouched, two launches bitwise; the MTP matrix at every residue of the step-0
position on ~60-token sequences (the step-0-anchored oracle within budget; the per-row-tail reading 0.07-0.11 off on exactly the rows
that see a block completed after step 0, equal elsewhere); the block's form BITWISE the standalone adapter on the block's own Q / gate
views, pools, table and list (split 1 and 4); `get_workspace_size()` honest under a split (a sentinel past the carve untouched); the
FIRST execute of a fresh declaration captured into a CUDA graph on a new stream with no warm-up under `set_sync_debug_mode("error")`,
the replay bitwise eager, the replay over new lengths / tables / lists / slots / inputs bitwise eager.

Also on Rubin, at the head rebased onto develop's fused write-through (#1649) and live-token count (#1645) -- the decode module
32 passed again --: the serving modules (`test_block_serving_extend.py` / `_decode.py` / `_capture.py`: 177 passed, the fold's
and the live-count cells among them), the two QSA block modules (124 passed), the sparse kernel module (327 passed).  Host (an
A100, cc 8.0): the new module, the QSA block modules, the serving modules, the sparse module's host cells and the tier lists
353 passed / 452 skipped / 0 failed.  The API index gains the one row the appended envelope field adds
(`DecodeEnvelope.sparse_core`; no other export changes).

## Performance

Measured on ONE exclusive GPU of a 212-SM Rubin part (cc 10.7, 2376 MHz lock sampled every window, the clock-event counters' delta 0;
CUPTI per-kernel device medians, 3 rounds x 100 executes, slots shuffled per round, a control pair 0.65 % apart; every cell validated
against the oracle / the dense function before timing).  The Flash-Next 24 / 2 d256 geometry at `d_model` 2560, bf16, page 16 HND pools,
`fuse_norm_rope` + `fuse_gate` on both arms, random 512-lists at the step-0 position.  **baseline** = the block's DENSE decode form (the
Rubin d256 decode tile over the same pools, its own split model); **FROST** = the block-sparse decode mode (the sparse core reading the
pools; the fill rule's default split -- 8 on the B <= 4 cells (re-read after the cap below), 4 / 1 on the B = 32 cells).  Speed-ups are `baseline / FROST - 1`; **SOL % is against BYTES-HBM**: the
attention kernels' ideal bytes (sparse: the ids row + the gathered K / V rows of the listed blocks and the tail per sequence x KV head x
row, + the fp32 partials under a split; dense: `B x H_kv x S_kv x (K + V)`) over their device time against the part's HBM copy pin
(13179.3 GB/s).

The split sweep (4 x 32K x 1; the sparse arm): split 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 17 -> step 69.2 / 64.3 / 59.9 / 59.8 / 65.0 us (the core

cost grows with the partial count, hence the default's cap of 8.  Launch census: 5 device events per step on both arms (the fused
projection GEMM, the cache write, the attention kernel, its combine, the out GEMM; 4 when unsplit).  The whole step is GEMM-dominated
at these `M = B x S_q` (the two projection GEMMs 45-50 us on the forced 128-row tile), which is why the attention kernels' 1.2-28x gains
over the dense tile show as +5.9 % .. +1463 % at the step; a small-M tile route for the serving projections is the next lever (#1646).
Limits: one node class; device-time medians of back-to-back executes; the sparse ideal bytes omit Q / O / the slab (identical for both
arms); the B <= 4 rows were re-read at the shipped default (split 8) after the sweep set the cap -- at the pre-cap split 17 the same
cells read -2.8 % (4 x 2048 x 1) .. +126 % (4 x 128K x 1) at the step.

## Open items

* The in-block indexer's decode step (the step-0 selection over the compressed-key cache and the raw-key ring): a follow-up; a
  serving stack hands the step's list in.
* A caller who wants per-row lists at `S_q <= 4` has no declaration for it (the form follows `S_q`); an append-only `QsaSpec` field
  would be the way, once a stack asks.
* The band geometry's projection has no forced tile, so no capture-safe route (eager only) until the band is padded to 256 columns.
* The split combine's cost grows with the partial count (12 us at 17 chunks; the dense decode tile's own combine reads 20-42 us at its
  32 / 64-way splits): a combine-kernel lever, not touched here.

detail.body:
## Summary

The gated attention block serves the Flash-Next / QSA **decode step over a paged KV cache**: a dense `[B, S_q]` declaration on a
`QsaSpec` geometry (`causal_bottom_right=True`) with `kv_source="paged"`, `paged_kv_page_size=P` and the pools' and block table's
samples.  The step's tokens are written through into the pools (and the raw indexer key into `index_k_raw` when the band is declared),
then stage (4) is the Rubin index-list sparse core **reading the pools** (`sdpa/fwd/sparse_gqa_sm107`'s paged read on the
bottom-right diagonal): per sequence the listed 4-token blocks plus the open tail over the first `kv_lens[b]` tokens of
`block_table[b]`, row `j` at position `kv_lens[b] - S_q + j`.

* **The list form is a declaration fact derived from `S_q`.**  At `S_q <= 4` ONE list per sequence -- `execute(block_ids=)`
  `[B, top_k]` int32 (+ `block_lens [B]`), selected at the step-0 position `kv_lens[b] - S_q` and shared by the step's rows: a
  speculative (MTP) row sees the listed blocks plus every token from the step-0 tail start to its own position (the contract page's
  definition; the adapter's `list_per_sequence` arm).  Past four rows one list per row (`[B, S_q, top_k]` / `[B x S_q, top_k]`) at
  bottom-right positions: a chunked prefill / prefix-cache hit over the pools, at any `S_q` (the sparse core runs one work item per
  query row: no 32-row cap, no decode-tile route).
* **`decode_split_kv`** is the one performance knob: `None` = the fill rule `ceil(SMs / (B x H_kv x S_q))` capped at the item's
  tile count `ceil((top_k + 1) / 32)`, or a pinned int in that range; fp32 partials inside `get_workspace_size()`, the split combine
  as a second launch; the same function under every value.  `fuse_gate` is served at every split (the core's epilogue unsplit, the
  combine otherwise); `return_lse` is served (`[B, H_q, S_q]` fp32).
* **Typed declines** (each naming its feature, every one pinned): the packed (`thd=True`) form over the pools -- the serving table's
  `sparse` row now reads "the sparse core serves packed sequences and paged pools one at a time"; a block-table sample that is not
  contiguous (the core binds the whole `[B, max_pages]` table; `execute(block_table=)` is exactly that table); a split past the
  item's tile count; `fuse_prepare`; the in-block indexer over the pools; `causal_bottom_right` on the block's own K / V now names
  this mode.  `_EXTEND_DECLINES`' `decode_rows` and `return_lse` rows exempt `QsaSpec` geometries; `serving_envelope(...).decode`
  gains `sparse_core` (appended) and spells both list forms in `requires`; `routes` is empty for a sparse geometry (the dense tile's
  facts do not apply).
* **Two execute-path details the cells caught**: at `S_q = 1` torch's `.view` gives the unit seq dim a stride that differs from the
  declared one and the adapter's exact `_bind` refused it -- the sparse stage now re-strides UNIT dims of its bound views to the
  declaration (an exact view; a non-unit mismatch stays the typed refusal); the serving declaration's capture-safe projections exist
  only for an `N` that 256 divides, so the indexer band (+640 columns) keeps the driver's route (eager steps; a capture is the
  driver's typed refusal at the first captured execute) instead of declining the whole block at compile.
* **The MTP matrix of the standalone sparse decode form** (the kernel-side cells cut out of the sparse-core PR as planned): every
  residue of the step-0 position at `S_q` 1..4, the shared list bitwise the replicated per-token list plus the completed block
  appended explicitly, the `S_q = 5` boundary decline, and the tracker's MTP wording with the bytes per step.

No kernel, barrier, ring or SMEM change: the mode binds the sparse core's served arms (`bottom_right` / `list_per_sequence` /
`split_kv` / `paged_kv`).  The `SparseCapabilities` record's fields do not move (its `decode` comment names the block); the
tracker's serving-forms section, index-list section, feature row and gaps rows and the doc page's contract table, decode-mode
paragraph, decode-form section and limits bullets flip in the same commit.

## Tests

`test/python/gated_attention_block/cutedsl/test_block_qsa_decode.py` (new, L0).  Host cells (any device): the declaration facts
(the list form per `S_q`, no dense route, where the gate runs, the split rule, the capture-safe projections per geometry), the typed
declines, the static envelope, the execute-time form checks on an uncompiled block under `set_sync_debug_mode("error")` (the 16-byte
base-alignment refusal of `block_ids` before any stage on both list forms, with an aligned storage-offset control -- a review item), the split
rule.  Rubin cells (cc 10.7, a development node, 204 SMs; functional, no perf claim): the decode ladder -- 9 cells, `S_q` 1..4 shared
and 8 / 64 per row, `B` 1 / 2 / 4, `kv_lens` 2 .. 20000 with a dead entry and a sequence shorter than the step, pages 16 / 32 / 64
on HND / NHD / unified pools, bf16 / f16, splits 1 / 2 / 4 / 17 and the rule, the gate fused and separate, the LSE, the indexer
band's raw-key write-through, the 24 / 2 geometry at `d_model` 2560 -- against the fp32 oracle of the WHOLE sequence (the dense block
reference's post-norm / post-RoPE Q, K, V and gate; the prefix rows fill NaN pools, the step rows are the block's own write-through;
the step rows' attention over `qsa_visible_mask(..., pos0=)`): `cos(out) >= 0.99998`, the gated O within 3.9e-3 bf16 / 3.1e-5 f16
(the suite's `atol 2e-2`, never widened), the LSE within 7.3e-5, dead rows exactly `0` / `-inf`, the pools' step rows BITWISE the
slab's K / V bands, the prefix rows and the NULL block untouched, two launches bitwise; the MTP matrix at every residue of the step-0
position on ~60-token sequences (the step-0-anchored oracle within budget; the per-row-tail reading 0.07-0.11 off on exactly the rows
that see a block completed after step 0, equal elsewhere); the block's form BITWISE the standalone adapter on the block's own Q / gate
views, pools, table and list (split 1 and 4); `get_workspace_size()` honest under a split (a sentinel past the carve untouched); the
FIRST execute of a fresh declaration captured into a CUDA graph on a new stream with no warm-up under `set_sync_debug_mode("error")`,
the replay bitwise eager, the replay over new lengths / tables / lists / slots / inputs bitwise eager.

Also on Rubin, at the head rebased onto develop's fused write-through (#1649) and live-token count (#1645) -- the decode module

and the live-count cells among them), the two QSA block modules (124 passed), the sparse kernel module (327 passed).  Host (an
A100, cc 8.0): the new module, the QSA block modules, the serving modules, the sparse module's host cells and the tier lists
353 passed / 452 skipped / 0 failed.  The API index gains the one row the appended envelope field adds
(`DecodeEnvelope.sparse_core`; no other export changes).

## Performance

Measured on ONE exclusive GPU of a 212-SM Rubin part (cc 10.7, 2376 MHz lock sampled every window, the clock-event counters' delta 0;
CUPTI per-kernel device medians, 3 rounds x 100 executes, slots shuffled per round, a control pair 0.65 % apart; every cell validated

pools; the fill rule's default split -- 8 on the B <= 4 cells (re-read after the cap below), 4 / 1 on the B = 32 cells).  Speed-ups are `baseline / FROST - 1`; **SOL % is against BYTES-HBM**: the

row, + the fp32 partials under a split; dense: `B x H_kv x S_kv x (K + V)`) over their device time against the part's HBM copy pin
(13179.3 GB/s).

+def _rope_tables(n_pos, dtype, ref_geom):
+    cos, sin = build_rope_tables(n_pos, ROPE, base=ref_geom.rope_base, batch=1, device=_DEV, dtype=dtype)

+class _Case:
+    """One sparse DECODE step over a batch of sequences with lengths ``kv_lens`` (0 = a dead entry; a length below ``s_q`` leaves
+    the rows with a negative position dead): the whole-sequence inputs per entry, the step's inputs (its last ``s_q`` positions),
+    the NaN-filled pools holding the ORACLE's prefix K / V, the block table (page 0 = the NULL block of a dead entry, ``-1`` past a
+    sequence's live pages), the slot mapping of the step's tokens (-1 on a dead row), the lists (one per sequence at the step-0
+    position, or one per row), and the per-sequence fp32 oracle of the step's ``out`` rows, gated O and LSE."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        geom_kw,
+        s_q,
+        kv_lens,
+        *,
+        page=16,
+        layout="hnd",
+        dtype=BF16,
+        seed=0,
+        top_k=512,
+        block_lens=True,
+        return_lse=False,
+        fuse_gate=False,
+        fuse_norm_rope=False,
+        split=None,
+        index_band=False,
+        n_pages=None,
+        pos0_anchor=True,
+        shuffle=True,
+    ):
+        self.s_q, self.kv_lens, self.page, self.layout, self.dtype, self.top_k = int(s_q), [int(x) for x in kv_lens], page, layout, dtype, top_k
+        self.block_lens_given, self.return_lse, self.fuse_gate, self.index_band = bool(block_lens), bool(return_lse), bool(fuse_gate), bool(index_band)
+        self.shared = self.s_q <= SHARED_MAX_S_Q
+        self.geom, self.ref_geom = _geom(geom_kw, top_k=top_k, index_band=index_band)
+        geom, ref_geom = self.geom, self.ref_geom
+        h_q, h_kv, d_model = geom.h_q, geom.h_kv, geom.d_model
+        G = h_q // h_kv
+        B = len(self.kv_lens)
+        g = torch.Generator(device=_DEV).manual_seed(seed)
+        self.gen = g
+
+        def randn(*shape, std=0.02):
+            return (torch.randn(*shape, generator=g, device=_DEV, dtype=torch.float32) * std).to(dtype)
+
+        n_dense = sum(geom.qkvg_block_widths[:4])
+        w_qkvg = randn(geom.n_qkvg, d_model)
+        self.w = dict(
+            w_qkvg=w_qkvg, w_q_norm=torch.ones(D, dtype=dtype, device=_DEV), w_k_norm=torch.ones(D, dtype=dtype, device=_DEV), w_o=randn(d_model, h_q * D)
+        )
+        L_max = max(max(self.kv_lens), s_q)
+        cos_t, sin_t = _rope_tables(L_max, dtype, ref_geom)
+        scale = geom.scale
+        # the step's inputs: row j of entry b is at position p_j = L - s_q + j; a negative position is a DEAD row (finite inputs, RoPE row 0)
+        self.h = torch.zeros(B, s_q, d_model, dtype=dtype, device=_DEV)
+        self.cos = cos_t[0, :1].expand(s_q, ROPE).clone()[None].expand(B, s_q, ROPE).clone()
+        self.sin = sin_t[0, :1].expand(s_q, ROPE).clone()[None].expand(B, s_q, ROPE).clone()
+        self.ref_out = torch.zeros(B, s_q, d_model, dtype=dtype, device=_DEV)
+        self.ref_o_gated = torch.zeros(B, s_q, h_q, D, dtype=dtype, device=_DEV)
+        self.ref_lse = torch.full((B, h_q, s_q), float("-inf"), dtype=torch.float32, device=_DEV)
+        self.ref_lse_rowtail = self.ref_lse.clone()
+        self.ref_o_gated_rowtail = self.ref_o_gated.clone()
+        self.ref_rows = {}
+        self.live_rows = torch.zeros(B, s_q, dtype=torch.bool, device=_DEV)
+        ids_rows, lens_rows = [], []
+        for b, L in enumerate(self.kv_lens):
+            pos = torch.arange(s_q, device=_DEV) + (L - s_q)
+            live = pos >= 0
+            self.live_rows[b] = live
+            pos0 = torch.tensor([L - s_q], device=_DEV)
+            if self.shared:
+                ids_b, lens_b = random_block_ids(pos0, top_k, BS, generator=g, kv_lens=torch.tensor([L], device=_DEV), shuffle=shuffle)
+            else:
+                ids_b, lens_b = random_block_ids(pos, top_k, BS, generator=g, kv_lens=torch.tensor([L], device=_DEV).expand(s_q), shuffle=shuffle)
+            ids_rows.append(ids_b)
+            lens_rows.append(lens_b)
+            if L == 0:
+                continue  # a dead entry: no sequence, no reference, block 0, slots -1
+            h_full = randn(1, L, d_model, std=1.0)
+            ref = gated_attention_block_reference(
+                h_full, w_qkvg[:n_dense], self.w["w_q_norm"], self.w["w_k_norm"], cos_t[:, :L], sin_t[:, :L], self.w["w_o"], ref_geom
+            )
+            self.ref_rows[b] = (ref.k[0], ref.v[0])  # [L, h_kv, D]: the prefix rows fill the pools
+            p_live = pos[live]
+            self.h[b, live] = h_full[0, p_live]
+            self.cos[b, live] = cos_t[0, p_live]
+            self.sin[b, live] = sin_t[0, p_live]
+            # the step rows' attention over the sequence's keys through the visible mask (the shared list anchored at pos_0, or per row)
+            rows = ids_b.expand(s_q, top_k) if self.shared else ids_b
+            lens_arg = (lens_b.expand(s_q) if self.shared else lens_b) if block_lens else None
+            q_rows = ref.q[0][p_live].float()  # [n_live, h_q, D]
+            gate_rows = ref.gate[0][p_live].float()
+            for anchored, (o_dst, lse_dst) in ((True, (self.ref_o_gated, self.ref_lse)), (False, (self.ref_o_gated_rowtail, self.ref_lse_rowtail))):
+                if not anchored and not self.shared:
+                    continue
+                allowed = qsa_visible_mask(rows, lens_arg, pos, L, L, BS, top_k=top_k, pos0=(L - s_q) if (anchored and self.shared) else None)[live]
+                o = torch.zeros(int(live.sum()), h_q, D, dtype=torch.float32, device=_DEV)
+                lse = torch.full((h_q, int(live.sum())), float("-inf"), dtype=torch.float32, device=_DEV)
+                for hh in range(h_q):
+                    kk, vv = ref.k[0][:, hh // G].float(), ref.v[0][:, hh // G].float()
+                    sc = (q_rows[:, hh] @ kk.t()) * scale
+                    sc = sc.masked_fill(~allowed, float("-inf"))
+                    rmax = sc.amax(dim=-1)
+                    dead = torch.isinf(rmax) & (rmax < 0)
+                    safe = torch.where(dead, torch.zeros_like(rmax), rmax)
+                    p = torch.where(allowed, torch.exp(sc - safe[:, None]), torch.zeros_like(sc))
+                    den = p.sum(dim=-1)
+                    den_safe = torch.where(dead, torch.ones_like(den), den)
+                    oc = (p @ vv) / den_safe[:, None]
+                    o[:, hh] = torch.where(dead[:, None], torch.zeros_like(oc), oc)
+                    lse[hh] = torch.where(dead, torch.full_like(den, float("-inf")), safe + torch.log(den))
+                o16 = o.to(dtype)  # the oracle's single rounding of O, then the gate in fp32, then one rounding
+                og = (o16.float() * torch.sigmoid(gate_rows)).to(dtype)
+                o_dst[b, live] = og
+                lse_dst[b, :, live] = lse
+                if anchored:
+                    self.ref_out[b, live] = (og.reshape(-1, h_q * D).float() @ self.w["w_o"].float().t()).to(dtype)
+        self.block_ids = torch.stack([x.reshape(top_k) if self.shared else x.reshape(s_q, top_k) for x in ids_rows]).contiguous()
+        self.block_lens = torch.stack([x.reshape(()) if self.shared else x.reshape(s_q) for x in lens_rows]).contiguous()
+        assert self.block_ids.dtype == torch.int32 and self.block_lens.dtype == torch.int32
+        # pages: block 0 reserved (NULL); each live entry gets ceil(L / P) pages from a permutation of 1 .. n_pages - 1; -1 past them
+        need = sum(-(-L // page) for L in self.kv_lens)
+        self.n_pages = n_pages if n_pages is not None else need + 1 + 2
+        assert self.n_pages >= need + 1, (self.n_pages, need)
+        perm = (torch.randperm(self.n_pages - 1, generator=g, device=_DEV) + 1).tolist()
+        self.max_pages = max(-(-L_max // page), 1)
+        self.block_table = torch.full((B, self.max_pages), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=_DEV)
+        it = iter(perm)
+        slots = torch.full((B * s_q,), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=_DEV)
+        self.k_cache, self.v_cache = _pools(self.n_pages, h_kv, page, layout, dtype)
+        self.index_cache = torch.full((self.n_pages, page, geom.qsa.index_head_dim), float("nan"), dtype=dtype, device=_DEV) if index_band else None
+        for b, L in enumerate(self.kv_lens):
+            if L == 0:
+                self.block_table[b] = 0  # the dead entry: the NULL block, slots -1
+                continue
+            pages = [next(it) for _ in range(-(-L // page))]
+            self.block_table[b, : len(pages)] = torch.tensor(pages, dtype=torch.int32, device=_DEV)
+            k_rows, v_rows = self.ref_rows[b]
+            for p in range(max(L - s_q, 0)):  # the PREFIX: the oracle's rows into the pools
+                pg, off = pages[p // page], p % page
+                self.k_cache[pg, :, off] = k_rows[p]
+                self.v_cache[pg, :, off] = v_rows[p]
+            for j in range(s_q):  # the step's live tokens: written through by the block
+                p = L - s_q + j
+                if p >= 0:
+                    slots[b * s_q + j] = pages[p // page] * page + p % page
+        self.slot_mapping = slots
+        self.kv_lens_t = torch.tensor(self.kv_lens, dtype=torch.int32, device=_DEV)
+        self.prefix_bits = (_bits(self.k_cache).clone(), _bits(self.v_cache).clone())
+        kw = dict(
+            paged_kv_page_size=page,
+            kv_source=KV_SOURCE_PAGED,
+            sample_k_cache=self.k_cache,
+            sample_v_cache=self.v_cache,
+            sample_block_table=self.block_table,
+            fuse_gate=fuse_gate,
+            fuse_norm_rope=fuse_norm_rope,
+            return_lse=return_lse,
+            decode_split_kv=split,

+        self.blk_kw = kw
+        self.out = torch.empty(B, s_q, d_model, dtype=dtype, device=_DEV)
+        self.lse = torch.empty(B, h_q, s_q, dtype=torch.float32, device=_DEV) if return_lse else None
+        self.blk = GatedAttentionBlockFwd(
+            self.h, self.w["w_qkvg"], self.w["w_q_norm"], self.w["w_k_norm"], self.cos, self.sin, self.w["w_o"], self.out, self.geom, **kw
+        )
+        assert isinstance(self.blk._sdpa, _SparseSdpa) and self.blk.sparse_decode and self.blk.qsa_shared_list is self.shared

+    def compile(self):
+        assert self.blk.check_support()
+        self.blk.compile()
+        self.ws = torch.full((self.blk.get_workspace_size(),), 0x7F, dtype=torch.uint8, device=_DEV)

+    def execute(
+        self, *, out=None, ws=None, lse=None, h=None, cos=None, sin=None, kv_lens=None, block_table=None, slot_mapping=None, ids=None, lens=None, stream=None

+            self.w["w_qkvg"],
+            self.w["w_q_norm"],

+            assert torch.equal(tail, (t >= tail_start) & (t <= pos_j)), f"seq {b} row {j}: the tail must be [{tail_start}, {pos_j}]"
+            assert pos_j // 4 - tail_start // 4 + 1 == n_tail[j], f"seq {b} row {j}: {pos_j // 4 - tail_start // 4 + 1} tail blocks, expected {n_tail[j]}"
+            assert not vis0[j][t > pos_j].any(), f"seq {b} row {j}: a key past the row's own position is visible"
+            # the two readings differ on exactly the teeth rows, by exactly block k; elsewhere the oracles coincide bitwise
+            differs = not torch.equal(vis0[j], vis_row[j])
+            assert differs == (
+                j in teeth_rows
+            ), f"seq {b} row {j}: readings {'differ' if differs else 'coincide'}, expected {'teeth' if j in teeth_rows else 'coincidence'}"
+            if differs:
+                hidden = vis0[j] & ~vis_row[j]
+                assert int(hidden.sum()) == 4 and not (vis_row[j] & ~vis0[j]).any() and int(hidden.nonzero().min()) == 4 * (pos0 // 4)
+                assert not torch.equal(ref_o[b, j], alt_o[b, j])
+            else:
+                assert torch.equal(ref_o[b, j], alt_o[b, j]) and torch.equal(ref_lse[b, :, j], alt_lse[b, :, j])
+        if L < 100:  # natural teeth on the short sequence: the hidden block's 4 keys weigh more than the budget
+            for j in teeth_rows:
+                d = float((o[b, j].float() - alt_o[b, j]).abs().max())
+                dl = float((lse[b, :, j] - alt_lse[b, :, j]).abs().max())
+                assert d > ATOL and dl > ATOL, f"seq {b} row {j} (pos {pos0 + j}): the hidden block k must weigh more than the budget ({d:.4f} / {dl:.4f})"
+                report.append(f"seq {b} row {j} teeth {d:.4f}/{dl:.4f}")
+        if b == b_long:  # the plant
+            margin = _plant_margin(q, k, b, j_plant, h_plant, G, pos_plant, vis0[j_plant], scale)
+            assert margin >= 8.0, f"plant margin {margin:.2f} nats"
+            v_plant = v[b, pos_plant, h_plant // G].float()
+            cos_p = float(torch.nn.functional.cosine_similarity(o[b, j_plant, h_plant].float(), v_plant, dim=0))
+            assert cos_p > 0.99, f"the plant row {j_plant} must attend its own token (cos {cos_p:.4f})"
+            for j in range(j_plant):  # per-row causal: the rows before the plant row never see it
+                assert not vis0[j, pos_plant] and not vis_row[j, pos_plant]
+                d = float((o[b, j, h_plant].float() - v_plant).abs().max())
+                assert d >= 10 * ATOL, f"row {j} sits at {d:.4f} from the planted V: a future key leaked"
+            if j_plant in teeth_rows:  # the 4k + 3 row sees block k, which the per-row-tail reading hides
+                assert bool(vis0[j_plant, pos_plant]) and not bool(vis_row[j_plant, pos_plant])
+                d = float((o[b, j_plant, h_plant].float() - alt_o[b, j_plant, h_plant]).abs().max())
+                cos_a = float(torch.nn.functional.cosine_similarity(o[b, j_plant, h_plant].float(), alt_o[b, j_plant, h_plant], dim=0))
+                assert cos_a < 0.5 and d >= 10 * ATOL, f"the 4k + 3 row must see block k: vs the per-row-tail oracle cos {cos_a:.3f}, diff {d:.4f}"
+                report.append(
+                    f"plant row {j_plant} (4k+3, pos {pos_plant}): margin {margin:.1f} nats, cos {cos_p:.4f} with V, vs per-row-tail cos {cos_a:.3f} diff {d:.3f}"
+                )
+            else:
+                assert bool(vis0[j_plant, pos_plant]) and bool(vis_row[j_plant, pos_plant])
+                where = "a listed complete block" if plant_listed else "the open block"
+                report.append(f"plant row {j_plant} (last row, pos {pos_plant}, {where}): margin {margin:.1f} nats, cos {cos_p:.4f} with V")
+    if B == 1:  # MTP x split
+        sp = _launch_decode(q, (k, v), ids, lens, kv_lens, top_k, scale, split=2, launches=1)
+        _check([(sp[0][0], sp[0][1])], ref_o, ref_lse)
+        live = ~torch.isinf(ref_lse).permute(0, 2, 1)
+        d, ratio = _split_vs_unsplit(sp[0][0].float(), o.float(), dtype, pv_abs, live)
+        lse_d = float((sp[0][1] - lse)[~torch.isinf(ref_lse)].abs().max())
+        assert ratio <= 1.0 and lse_d <= ATOL, f"split 2 vs unsplit: {ratio:.3f} of the derived budget, |dLSE| {lse_d:.2e}"
+        extra = f"; split2 vs unsplit {d:.3e} = {ratio:.3f} of the budget"
+    else:  # MTP x paged
+        P, hnd = (16, True) if S_q % 2 == 0 else (64, False)
+        kp, vp, table = _paginate(k, v, kv_lens, P, hnd, "nan", g)
+        pg = _launch_decode(q, (kp, vp, table, P), ids, lens, kv_lens, top_k, scale, split=1, launches=1)
+        _check([(pg[0][0], pg[0][1])], ref_o, ref_lse)
+        _assert_bitwise((pg[0][0], pg[0][1]), (o, lse), f"MTP S_q {S_q} r {r} paged page {P} {'HND' if hnd else 'NHD'}")
+        extra = f"; paged {P} {'HND' if hnd else 'NHD'} bitwise the dense read"
+    print(
+        f"\nMTP matrix S_q={S_q} r={r} B={B} lens={kv_lens}: max|dO| {max_o:.5f} max|dLSE| {max_lse:.6f}; n_tail {n_tail}; teeth rows {teeth_rows}; "
+        + "; ".join(report)
+        + extra
+    )
+
+
+def _per_token_lists_from_shared(ids_seq, lens_seq, kv_lens, S_q):
+    """The per-token bottom-right lists that spell the SHARED-list semantics explicitly: row ``j`` of sequence ``b`` = the step-0 list
+    (its ``count`` entries, replicated) + the block completed between ``pos_0`` and ``pos_j`` (``floor((pos_j + 1) / 4) - tail_lo``: 0 or
+    1 at ``S_q <= 4``) appended at index ``count``; ``block_lens`` = ``count`` + that.  The kernel derives the row's own open block in
+    both forms, so the tiles hold the same blocks in the same order.  Needs ``count + 1 <= top_k`` (clamp ``lens_seq`` first)."""
+    B, top_k = ids_seq.shape
+    ids3 = ids_seq[:, None, :].expand(B, S_q, top_k).clone()
+    lens2 = torch.zeros(B, S_q, dtype=torch.int32, device=ids_seq.device)
+    for b in range(B):
+        L = int(kv_lens[b])
+        pos0 = L - S_q
+        assert pos0 >= 0
+        count = min(max(int(lens_seq[b]), 0), min(top_k, (pos0 + 1) // 4))
+        tail_lo = min(pos0 + 1, L) // 4
+        for j in range(S_q):
+            n_between = (pos0 + j + 1) // 4 - tail_lo
+            assert 0 <= n_between <= 1 and count + n_between <= top_k
+            if n_between:
+                ids3[b, j, count] = tail_lo
+            lens2[b, j] = count + n_between
+    return ids3.contiguous(), lens2.contiguous()
+
+
+@requires_rubin
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("r", [0, 1, 2, 3], ids=[f"pos0-mod4-{r}" for r in range(4)])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("S_q", [2, 4], ids=["Sq2", "Sq4"])
+def test_decode_form_mtp_shared_list_is_bitwise_the_replicated_per_token_list(S_q, r):
+    """The step-0 reuse pin: the shared-list form is BITWISE the per-token bottom-right form (``block_ids [B, S_q, top_k]``,
+    ``list_per_sequence=False``) fed with the step-0 list replicated on every row plus the block completed between ``pos_0`` and
+    ``pos_j`` appended explicitly (:func:`_per_token_lists_from_shared`) -- the drafted rows share ONE list, the appended tail ids
+    are exactly the derived ones and the count anchor is the step-0 position, or the two renderings would gather different tiles.
+    ``block_lens`` on the shared form is clamped to ``top_k - 2`` so the replicated row has room; sequences at ``56 + r + S_q`` (short)
+    and ``8192 + r + S_q`` (a saturated list), both within the budget vs the pos0 oracle."""
+    B, H, KH, top_k = 2, 24, 2, 512
+    dtype = torch.bfloat16
+    kv_lens = [56 + r + S_q, 8192 + r + S_q]
+    q, k, v, g = _inputs(B, S_q, H, KH, dtype, seed=200 + 4 * S_q + r, SKV=max(kv_lens))
+    ids, lens = _decode_lists("shuffled", B, S_q, top_k, kv_lens, g)
+    lens = torch.minimum(lens, torch.full_like(lens, top_k - 2)).contiguous()
+    scale = 1.0 / math.sqrt(D)
+    ref_o, ref_lse, _ = _reference_decode(q, k, v, ids, lens, kv_lens, scale, top_k)
+    shared = _launch_decode(q, (k, v), ids, lens, kv_lens, top_k, scale, split=1)
+    max_o, max_lse = _check([(o, l) for o, l, _ in shared], ref_o, ref_lse)
+    ids3, lens2 = _per_token_lists_from_shared(ids, lens, kv_lens, S_q)
+    appended = int((lens2 > lens[:, None]).sum())
+    assert appended == B * len(
+        [j for j in range(S_q) if r < 3 and r + j >= 3]
+    ), "a block is appended exactly on the rows where the per-row-tail reading would hide one"
+    per_tok = _launch_decode(q, (k, v), ids3, lens2, kv_lens, top_k, scale, split=1, launches=1, list_per_sequence=False)
+    _check([(per_tok[0][0], per_tok[0][1])], ref_o, ref_lse)
+    _assert_bitwise((per_tok[0][0], per_tok[0][1]), (shared[0][0], shared[0][1]), f"S_q {S_q} r {r}: the replicated per-token list vs the shared list")
+    print(
+        f"\nshared list == replicated per-token list (bitwise) S_q={S_q} r={r} lens={kv_lens}: max|dO| {max_o:.5f} max|dLSE| {max_lse:.6f}; rows with an appended block {appended}"
+    )
